problem: The sentence reads "If p0.5 it has a longer left tail." The comparison sign has been lost, so the sentence states no condition, and as printed it also leaves out the rule for p<0.5 — which is exactly the case (p=0.2) used in the worked example and quiz. A student would carry away a wrong or empty skew rule.
fix: Write both cases: "At p = 0.5 the pmf is symmetric: P(X = k) = P(X = n − k). If p < 0.5 the pmf is skewed right, with a longer right tail. If p > 0.5 it is skewed left, with a longer left tail."

problem: "point binomial" is normally the name for the single-trial Bernoulli distribution, not for Bin(n, p). Listing it as another name for the binomial count can confuse a student who meets the term elsewhere.
fix: "Some syllabi call it the Bernoulli counting distribution." Drop "point binomial", or say the single trial version is sometimes called the point binomial.

problem: The note "success = fail" reads like a contradiction on its own: it means the trial's "success" is defined as a failed payment, but the wording does not say so.
fix: Change the note to "success = payment fails" (or "success means fail"), so the definition of success is explicit.
